messages.content: How much electricity will I need for my 2000 sq ft home?

function.name: solar_panel_calculate_need
function.description: Calculate the number of solar panels needed for a house based on the square footage and average sunlight hours. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

square_footage.description: The square footage of the house. This is a float type value.

average_sunlight_hours.description: The average hours of sunlight received. This is a float type value.

usage_efficiency.description: The efficiency of energy usage in the home, default is 0.8. This is a float type value.

message.content:
A good rule‑of‑thumb for a typical U.S. home is **about 5 kWh of electricity per square foot per month** (≈ 60 kWh per 1,000 sq ft).  
For a 2,000 sq ft house that works out to roughly:

| Time period | Electricity needed |
|-------------|--------------------|
| **Monthly** | ≈ 10 000 kWh ÷ 12 ≈ **833 kWh** |
| **Yearly**  | **≈ 10 000 kWh** |

So you can expect to use on the order of **10 kWh per square foot per year**, which translates to about **10,000 kWh per year** for a 2,000 sq ft home.

> **Why this range?**  
> • Climate (cold vs. hot) – heating/cooling loads vary widely.  
> • Insulation & windows – better insulation reduces consumption.  
> • Appliances & electronics – high‑efficiency appliances lower usage.  
> • Occupancy patterns – more occupants or longer stays increase demand.  

If you’re looking to size a solar‑panel system for that load, let me know your average daily sunlight hours and any efficiency assumptions you’d like to use, and I can run the calculation for you.
